en: The Praise of the Auspicious Virtues of the Buddha, Volume One.
Composed by the Venerable Śāntimitra;
translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, the Court-Attendant Grand Master [of the Hanlin Academy].
I now take refuge in the Buddha, the World-Honored One, praising his supreme virtues:
his timely speech, truthful speech, and non-deceptive speech; his speech of reality, his speech of Dharma, and his speech according to the meaning;
his right speech, tranquil speech, and speech of non-self, which reveals the gateway to the ultimate truth.
Manifesting all bodies with eyes everywhere, Skillfully bestowing light and constantly observing,
Opening the eyes of wisdom for all sentient beings, Shattering all the darkness of their ignorance,
Truly giving birth from the Ten Powers, Having already reached the supreme ground of cool serenity.
Fully endowed with the four fearlessnesses and other virtues, He creates great radiance, holding aloft a torch;
He unfolds the blazing flames, spreading light everywhere, Bestowing upon others a magnificent mass of great brilliance,
Arousing firm and vigorous application of energy, Never diminishing any supreme merit.
The Lion of the Śākyas, with a great lion’s roar, is able to proclaim the unconditioned True Dharma;
he cannot be defiled by the eight worldly dharmas. This supreme, pure, and greatly compassionate one is revered by Brahmā, Śakra, Vaiśravaṇa, and all other devas.
Our Buddha constantly utters wondrous and skillful speech, Sweet, profound, and yet vast;
The sound of liberation through the principle of true suchness, Capable of understanding all languages.
Vast and pure as space, He was born into the royal palace of the most noble lineage.
The Buddha’s radiance is like that of the sun and moon; Devas, humans, and asuras make offerings to him.
Having attained the wondrous jewels of the seven factors of enlightenment, He erects the supreme banner of the Dharma-treasure.
The darkness and obscurations of ignorance are all dispelled and clarified, As his body shines with a mass of golden light.
The most supreme among men, the most honored among men, who has severed the defilements of greed, hatred, and delusion;
he is the *puṇḍarīka* flower among men, the various wondrous lotuses among men.
Purifying the sorrows, griefs, and afflictions of birth and death, ignorance and pride are entirely eliminated;
the gates of combat and contention are forever closed, and the various seeds of defilement in the continuum are eternally severed.
Bestowing all dharmas without secrecy or stinginess, you topple the banner of pride and erect the banner of Dharma;
you turn the wheel of the True Dharma to benefit sentient beings, shatter the wheel of birth and death, and bring rest to all sufferings.
The water of śamatha is limpid and pure, Like the ocean’s flow, deep and bottomless;
Having already dried up the source and currents of craving, It is thus filled with the waters of merit.
All who behold it give rise to a heart of joy, Remaining unattached in all places.
Able to sacrifice their own bodies for the sake of sentient beings, they are entirely impartial toward both enemies and kin.
Their complexion is like pure gold freshly emerged from the flames; their tongues are like lotuses, broad and pure.
The radiance of their bodies shines with brilliant clarity, as intense as gold and like a flash of lightning.
Vigorous exertion and diligent application form the waist; dwelling securely in samādhi forms the neck;
and penetrating wisdom forms the crown of the head—these manifest in succession as the marks of adornment.
The Tathāgata, the courageous and fearless Honored One, has fully penetrated all that is vast and far-reaching;
he can subdue the great elephants and dragons of Māra’s power and skillfully expounds the supreme words of all dharmas.
Abiding securely in the bliss of supreme and wondrous patience, having severed all bonds of craving,
established in right knowledge with firm wisdom, his insight is profound and vast, a wisdom that cannot be shattered.
The most supreme and rare udumbara flower possesses hundreds of thousands of kinds of sublime merit;
likewise, it is difficult to encounter the Tathāgata, the Holy Honored One, who is fully endowed with boundless dharmas of merit.
Like the earth which can support all seeds, he is stable, tranquil, and vast.
The wisdom of the Tathāgata is likewise so: Endowed with infinite qualities and dharmas,
Stainless, untainted, and fundamentally pure, This Honored One, having bathed body and mind and attained self-mastery,
Guides sentient beings toward the practice that reaches the further shore.
Fully endowed with the thirty-two marks, further adorned with the eighty secondary characteristics,
this supreme and wondrous body, perfected by a hundred merits, is vast, most excellent, and beyond compare.
Having attained mastery over all phenomena, He reveals the gateway to the pure ultimate truth;
Wisdom pervades all objective realms, And the vajra of wisdom shatters all afflictions.

Having already been able to subdue the objects of the world, And having awakened to the realization that the nature of hope has been eliminated, The remedies for afflictions are exhausted without remainder; Your vast eloquence is unimpeded.
Generosity, ethical discipline, and patience, Vigor, meditative concentration, and wisdom—
Having perfected all the pāramitās, The seer Asita constantly made offerings to him.
The Buddha is a mountain of sublime merit, a treasury of merit and an ocean of merit;
his self-awakening and awakening of others bring the practice of awakening to perfection. His voice resounds throughout the ten directions, shaking them all;
with boundless speech and boundless virtues, his eloquence is inexhaustible and limitless.
The Buddha, the Omniscient One, the Unsurpassed Honored One— I take refuge in the Buddha as the one of great kindness;
I take refuge in the well-doer who protects the world, Who has heard all dharmas according to their nature.
Having personally realized all gateways to the Dharma through your own wisdom, I bow my head to you, the most supreme knower of phenomena.
First, having perceived all phenomena with your own wisdom, you attained the unsurpassed, great Bodhi;
subsequently, you awakened sentient beings for their benefit in the same way. I bow my head to you, the one who has truly awakened for both self and others.
Truly understanding all holy practices (brahmacarya), unbroken and unsevered, with physical strength firm and steadfast,
endowed with purity and perfect in every way— I bow my head to those who purely cultivate the holy life.
Abiding securely in the quality of non-forgetfulness, the most supreme Honored One is courageous and steadfast;
the Buddha-mind is vast and its measure boundless, able to fully illuminate and penetrate the nature of both suffering and joy.
The Buddha is the most supreme and skillful tamer, Also called the Unsurpassed Honored One among Two-legged Beings;
Among all śramaṇas, he is the Great Śramaṇa; I prostrate to the Śramaṇa who is beyond reproach.
The Buddha has fully cultivated all pure practices, And is able to act as the Great Physician-King of the world;
Furthermore, he is the Honored One of Supreme Vision and Liberation— I bow my head to the Teacher of Great Wisdom.
Tamed, tranquil, and closely serene, Abiding in the supreme mind of discipline,
Having entered the gateway to the ultimate truth, I prostrate to you who have reached the ground of coolness.
All join their palms in reverent homage; You should receive the foremost offerings of gods and humans.
Worthy to be a field of merit for the gift of gods and humans, I take refuge in the Unsurpassed One, the Source of Blessings.
Knowing the Dharma, knowing the meaning, and knowing the measure of time; knowing reality as it is for oneself and for others;
fully understanding the faculties and natures of both self and others; and thoroughly discerning these and those who are transmigrating beings.
In samāhita, the faculties are stilled; all activities and deeds are fully perfected.
Possessing the complete precepts, they are wondrous and without flaw. I prostrate to the Great Power Samādhi.
Abiding in the samādhi of non-extinction, free from affliction, immovable, and beyond all peril;
having abandoned the mind of high and low or acceptance and rejection, one is forever detached from the continuity of rebirth.
With a mind as firm and stable as Mount Sumeru, one fully accomplishes the wisdom of non-retrogression.
Wisdom constantly follows throughout all places; I prostrate to the one with unsurpassed and unceasing wisdom.
Thoroughly knowing that all phenomena are invincible, the Buddha is the Honored One of loving vision and excellent insight.
His wisdom, love, and virtuous love are boundless; I prostrate to the one who is equal toward love and hatred.
Adored by the multitude for his supreme deportment, Possessing all exquisite and wondrous eloquence, His eloquence at will shatters ignorance; I prostrate to the one who proclaims the authentic word.
His fame is vast and most rare, heard everywhere throughout the three realms;
when the wise of the world question him according to their inquiries, the Buddha always answers skillfully without concealment.
The Buddha’s majestic deportment is supreme and peerless; All who behold him give rise to a heart of joy and contentment.
He causes all in the world to feel love and delight; I bow my head to the one who bestows happiness.
Swift in speech, without redundancy; equal, peerless, and without distinction;
possessing the flavor of perfection in wondrous sounds—homage to the one whose speech is unequaled.
The Buddha is the great wise one among men, And the supreme sage among the highest of humans;
In this world, no divergent views arise within him— I bow my head to him who has distanced himself from false thoughts and perceptions.

Having stilled all sorrows, lamentations, and afflictions, And having eliminated defiled phenomena without remainder, The faults of frivolity and agitation no longer arise; I prostrate to the one who has forever transcended all failings.
When reviled by the Tathāgata, his mind does not sink; when praised by the Tathāgata, his mind does not exult.
Equal toward both praise and blame, his wisdom remains serene. I prostrate to him who is unattached to slander or eulogy.
Whether level or uneven, defiled or pure, In suffering or joy, in love or hate— The Buddha’s wisdom is unattached and without distinction; I prostrate to the Tathāgata, the one of skillful speech.
Sentient beings speak evil words that are meaningless and of no benefit; the Tathāgata skillfully conceals them rather than exposing them.
He practices various acts of giving and gathers in the world; I prostrate to the Truly Real One, the Master of Speech.
Though reviled by wicked people with harsh words, the Buddha’s mind remains unmoved and serene;
regarding kind speech and evil speech as equal without distinction, I prostrate to the one who is impartial toward both love and hatred.
Gold, lapis lazuli, and precious gems—these are the most supreme treasures in the world;
yet the Tathāgata has already abandoned all craving and attachment, regarding them as equal to grass, wood, earth, and stone.
The Tathāgata has already abandoned the three types of pride; his mind is stable and serene.
Whether it be bedding, seats, or various treasures, he bestows them all upon those who come to seek them.
Neither rejoicing in gain nor feeling anger at loss, Even when treated with contempt, you give rise to a heart of joy and equanimity;
Free from sorrow and affliction, no faults arise— I bow my head to the Wise One who destroys false teachings.
Having already been able to distance oneself from all afflictions, one always speaks of associating with virtuous people;
one does not speak of worldly gain or profit, nor are there any words of falsehood or the like.
One's speech is spontaneous and masterful, and one’s discourse is tranquil and free from the pursuit of pleasure.
Your speech is purely one, immaculate and without flaw; I bow my head to you whose speech is tranquil.
Your speech is sweet and free from attachment; your speech can subdue all Māras.
Your speech is definitive and transcends the world; I bow my head to you who have already abandoned all ignorance.
Having already been able to distance yourself from inverted views, Having already abandoned frivolous and agitated conditions,
And having left behind all that is non-verbal, I prostrate to the one who gathers and transforms beings through excellent speech.
Always practicing without guile or deceit, Acting in accordance with a pure and true mind,
Extensively practicing love and respect that are truly without falsehood— I bow my head to those who have already crossed over the perils of birth and death.
All deeds are perfectly accomplished; this is the gateway from which the True Dharma arises.
To the World-Honored One whom all who see him rejoice, the Pure Being—to you I bow my head and take refuge.
I take refuge in the Teacher who personally proclaimed the teachings of all dharmas; Who, according to what is appropriate, turns away from afflictions and eliminates them;
Who correctly and excellently understands the gateway to renunciation; And who proceeds toward the realization of the true dharma of Bodhi.
The unassailable, sublime Dharma toward which one should turn, Which skillfully opens the gate of world-transcending peace and purity;
Even unto its perfect, wondrous, and extensive proclamation— This is the Dharma that brings benefit and happiness to gods and humans in the world.
The Tathāgata’s words on all phenomena are free from the sounds of attachment to desire;
having utterly eliminated all unrefined sounds, I prostrate to the one who skillfully teaches the Dharma.
The Tathāgata has long cultivated all forms of pure livelihood; His mind is free from agitation and fundamentally serene.
With mindfulness established in the three equalities, I prostrate to the Muni, who possesses the three things that need no guarding.
The Buddha has severed all speech of doubt; he constantly acts within the state of equanimity.
He is the unsurpassed gateway of love, wherein nirvāṇa is no different [from saṃsāra]. I prostrate to the one who has realized this vastness.
The Buddha is the supreme and most excellent guide, Endowed with all virtues, honored by devas and humans;
His supernormal powers and skillful means are fully perfected— I prostrate to him who has attained all masteries.
I prostrate and take refuge in the One of Perfect Virtues, Whose ten titles are fully realized and who is peerless;
In the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, The One Endowed with Knowledge and Conduct, the Sugata, The Knower of the World,
the Unsurpassed Being, The Charioteer of Men, and the Teacher of Gods and Humans.
The Buddha, the World-Honored One, is universally extolled; therefore, I now offer praise and prostration.
The Tathāgata is unstained and beyond awakening; born free from the womb, he is of supreme birth.
He can fulfill all the aspirations and requests of sentient beings; I bow my head to him who skillfully gathers all dharmas.
Manifesting birth in the pure lineage of a noble wheel-turning king, vast in wealth and status, and yet most exalted;
you are able to renounce it all and go forth into homelessness—homage to you who humble the mind and abandon arrogance.
Fully endowed with the supreme power of all forms, Your dignified marks and signs bring joy to all who see;
Having utterly renounced all the wondrous objects of the world, I prostrate to you, the one of pure liberation.
With precepts pure and complete without flaw, you are able to preach and act accordingly;
O Great Wisdom, Great Intelligence, Great Holy Honored One, I bow my head to the one who gathers and benefits others through shared activities.
The Buddha’s words are perfectly pure, bright, and further wondrously excellent; having severed craving, faults do not arise.
All defiled phenomena are entirely eliminated, as he proclaims the words of the true cause and right action.
The speech concerning all conditioned phenomena is free from entanglement;
always proclaiming with gentle and affectionate words, among the assemblies of śramaṇas and brāhmaṇas, the Tathāgata’s speech is always preeminent.
With a face perfectly round and free from frowns, you proceed with right conduct and remain serene;
you gather sentient beings with kind words of welcome and bow to you who correctly teach and subdue all faults.
All the speech you utter is perfect; your fearless vocal karma is well-praised.
With profound words, correct speech, and the language of wisdom, I bow my head to the Tathāgata who has stilled all harsh speech.
The Buddha’s speech is without attachment and without dependence, Nor does it contradict any form of language;
All its utterances are entirely boundless— I prostrate to the one who can expound the definitive meaning.
With skillful and beautiful speech and excellent eloquence, you bring benefit and joy through compassion for all sentient beings;
you extensively open the gates of discipline for all beings—to the Noble One who disciplines through the nature of phenomena, I pay homage.
The Buddha is the gentleman who tames through the True Dharma; The Honored One who tames all dharmas free from dust;
The Teacher who tames through peerless Dharma-gates; The Tamer who employs immeasurable dharmas.
The Tathāgata is perfectly equal in the fulfillment of ethical discipline; likewise, there is no difference in the fulfillment of concentration and wisdom.
The fulfillment of liberation is fundamentally of one source, and the fulfillment of the knowledge and vision of liberation is without distinction.
The Noble, Right, and Auspicious Great Awakened One, The supreme tamer who shares a single gateway,
Constantly rests all conditions within the forest wilds, Dwelling in peace, sitting or reclining as he pleases.
He teaches the Dharma through the characteristic of non-harming; he teaches the Dharma through the characteristic of absence of frivolous speech;
he teaches the Dharma through the characteristic of immovability; he teaches the Dharma by demonstrating the characteristic of renunciation;
he teaches the Dharma through the characteristic of having severed saṃsāra; he teaches the Dharma through the characteristic of the desirable nirvāṇa.
He teaches the Dharma without the characteristic of other suffering; he teaches the Dharma with the characteristic of the excellence of intrinsic nature;
he teaches the Dharma with the characteristic of benefiting the world; he teaches the Dharma with the characteristic of being free from false views;
he teaches the Dharma with the characteristic of the commonality of ordinary beings; he teaches the Dharma with the characteristic of non-continuity.
I prostrate to the one who teaches the Dharma without abiding in signs;
whether it be the phenomena or the wisdom, they are truly thus. You proclaim the definitive meaning to shatter doubt, teaching the Dharma with perfect clarity and skillful discernment.
You universally proclaim the truth, treating the high and the low with equality.
The right path and the false paths are both clearly revealed; Beneficial and non-beneficial matters are all well understood.
Whether wholesome or unwholesome, all are distinguished; One penetrates the gates of the true teaching and the false teachings.
With merit perfected and faults eliminated, I bow my head to the one who can deliver both self and others.
Able to destroy the evil realms through wholesome dharmas, Skillfully teaching that which is not true bliss within the midst of pleasure,
Truly knowing the arising and ceasing of the world, He excellently expounds the most supreme jewel of all dharmas.
The Tathāgata’s true and supreme teaching can accomplish all that is to be done within the three realms;
it fully understands both the happy and miserable destinies, and possesses non-erroneous wisdom regarding matters of good and evil.
Having realized the primordial nature of bondage and liberation, you are able to skillfully expound the gateways of bondage and liberation;
you fully comprehend both the false and the correct, as well as defilement and purity, and clearly understand the meaning of both the wholesome and the unwholesome.
Having already perfected the most supreme goodness, the Tathāgata—
whose compassionate action is universally extolled and who rescues all from within the evil realms— possesses compassion as his singular medicinal elixir.
I prostrate to the supreme being among celestial seers, who does not cling to the bliss of profound meditative concentration,
nor give rise to a mind of attachment or delight, but vows to deliver the ignorant and deluded from the ocean of craving.
Your own vast and manifold physical forms are ultimately perfect and worthy of praise;
O Supreme Honored One of the Three Realms, Worthy of Offerings, I now take refuge in you, the inconceivable.
Praise of the Auspicious Qualities of the Buddha, Volume One;
Praise of the Auspicious Qualities of the Buddha, Volume Two.
Composed by the Venerable Śāntamitra.

Translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, Imperial Meritorious Official Guiming, in homage to the Tathāgata’s supreme and wondrous marks: The soles of his feet are level and full, resting in perfect stability;
Upon the centers of his feet appear the patterns of thousand-spoked wheels, With all their rims and hubs complete in every detail.
His hands and feet are as soft as *tūla* cotton; A webbed lattice shines between his fingers and toes.
The fingers of his hands and feet are exquisite, slender, and long; His heels are full and his insteps are well-proportioned.
His insteps are high, elongated, and perfectly filled; His calves are like those of the *eṇeya* deer king.
His two arms are long and rounded, reaching down to his kneecaps; his private organs are concealed within a sheath like those of a dragon-horse.
The tips of his body hairs are glossy and all curl upward; each hair grows individually and spirals to the right.
His skin is fine and smooth, impervious to dust or grime; his body is the color of pure gold, radiating brilliant light.
The seven parts—the hands, feet, neck, and shoulders—are full; the nape of the neck, shoulders, and armpits are all well-filled and rounded.
His countenance is grave and majestic, exquisitely dignified; his physical marks are long and broad, moreover straight and upright.
Like the nyagrodha tree, his body is perfectly proportioned; the upper half of his body is like that of a lion king.
The constant radiance of his face extends one fathom in every direction; his forty teeth are even, neither sparse nor missing.
His four canine teeth are brilliant white and wonderfully sharp; he always attains the most supreme of flavors.
His tongue is thin, pure, broad, and long; his Brahma-voice is deep and wondrous, like a celestial drum.
All who hear his voice find it pleasing; it is further like the song of the kalaviṅka bird.
His eyelashes are even and well-proportioned like those of a bull king; his eyes are bright and pure, a deep azure-blue.
Between his brows is a soft and wondrous tuft of hair, curling to the right, as pure and white as a conch shell.
With the *uṣṇīṣa* adorning his crown, I bow my head to the one endowed with the marks of a Great Man (*mahāpuruṣa*).
I take refuge in the Tathāgata’s secondary characteristics (*anuvyañjana*): his fingernails are narrow and long like red copper;
his fingers and toes are rounded, slender, and elongated; and all his digits are perfectly proportioned.
The sinews and veins are coiled and deeply hidden; both ankles are concealed and not prominent.
The feet are full, soft, and level. He turns his gaze to the right like a king of deer;
his gait proceeds straight forward like that of an elephant king. He is radiant, dignified, and free from all obstruction.
Majestic in his gait like the king of geese, he moves with every limb following in turn; his body is steady and deliberate as it steps forward.
His physical parts are successively elevated and prominent, and as he moves with evenness, his body remains unbent.
His well-proportioned limbs form a solid and firm frame, and his body is pure and radiant, free from all obscurity or darkness.
The limbs of his body are stable and do not tremble; his upright physical form is perfectly complete.
His wondrous youthfulness and pure body are soft, exquisite, and entirely peerless.
The shape of his abdomen is square and regular, without deficiency; it is neither sunken nor protruding, but broad and round.
His navel-wheel is deep, thick, and spirals to the right; it is pure, without pores or blemishes, and never recedes downward.
His limbs are smooth to the touch and free from all defects; he is entirely without moles, spots, warts, or excrescences.
Like a lotus flower that cannot be defiled by impurity, he is likewise free from all states of unrest.
The circle of his face is perfectly full, bright, and pure; his physical marks are complete and without deficiency.
His tongue is broad and long like refined copper, soft and supple like a lotus petal.
The color of his lips is lustrous and lovely, like the *bimba* fruit or refined copper.

The sounds of water, clouds, and clashing instruments, And again like the great, thundering roar of a king of elephants— These voices are deep and far-reaching, yet exquisitely beautiful; All who hear them find their minds filled with joy.
His hands are as soft as *tūla* cotton, And the lines upon his palms are deep, clear, and unbroken.
The four canine teeth are sharp, wondrously firm, most supreme, pure, and perfectly even;
all the teeth are square, regular, fresh white, and aligned. The eyes are long and wide like lotus petals;
the eyelashes are dense and not white. The eyebrows are glossy, not white, and long.
The lobes of the ears are long, broad, thick, and round; each hair on the body is smooth and lustrous.
The forehead is wide, level, and upright, its features most exquisite; the upper half of the body is perfectly full and rounded.
The hair on the head is dense, well-ordered, and long; it is deep azure-blue, curling to the right, and radiant with gloss.
Extending even to the broad expanse of the Buddha’s chest, it is adorned with the auspicious mark of the whorl of joy;
his conch-like topknot is deep blue and exquisitely embellished—to the invisible crown of the head, I prostrate.
I take refuge in the power of knowledge regarding what is possible and impossible; You know all karma of the past, present, and future;
You understand the gates of dhyāna, liberation, and meditative concentration; You discern the various faculties of yourself and others;
You have thoroughly mastered all types of inclinations and understand all diverse realms of existence.
His knowledge of the minds of others is entirely without distinction; he is fully endowed with the wisdom of recollecting past lives.
He illuminates all phenomena of arising and ceasing; his outflows are exhausted, leaving none remaining.
Thus, his wisdom of the ten powers is perfect and complete; I prostrate to the Tathāgata of Great Diligence.
The Tathāgata has exhausted all outflows without remainder, And has awakened to all phenomena without remainder;
Therefore he is called the Honored One of Perfectly Equal and Perfect Enlightenment— I now bow my head to pay him respectful homage.
You have equally taught all defiled phenomena, and you have excellently proclaimed all paths of renunciation;
having fully awakened to everything without exception, I prostrate to the Muni, the first Awakened One.
The Buddha possesses indestructible, correct wisdom; as the Honored One of Manifest Awakening, he has universally realized all things without exception.
With correct wisdom, he destroys all minds of false wisdom; having attained true awakening, the Buddha has no further awakening to seek.
Regarding his own realm and the realms of others, he has accomplished the realization of all realms.
Among all things that constitute the objects of the senses, the Buddha is the faculty that is invincible.
Within his marks there is no further mark to be perceived; neither form nor its seeds, nor their manifestations, remain—everything is utterly severed.
The heavy burden of rebirth has long since been cast off, and he has reached the very bottom of the river of dependent origination.
Free from the two kinds of ignorance and the darkness of delusion, The light of the two kinds of wisdom arises;
Furthermore, free from the two kinds of doubting and seeking minds, The two kinds of definitive wisdom are established.
Having attained the worldly expression of the knowledge of exhaustion, With the cognitive obscurations already abandoned, the Dharma is perfectly luminous;
Fully endowed with the supreme basis of the gateway to tranquility, Fully endowed with the supreme stations and dwelling in perfect peace;
Fully endowed with all that is to be practiced, The perfection of knowledge and conduct, and the fullness of physical marks.
Fully endowed with spiritual lineage and language, Attaining the fruit of supernormal powers, they are skillful in salvation.
Their actions of body, speech, and mind require no protection; Unattached and inexhaustible, their wisdom is凝然 (tranquil and steadfast).
This is the gate of wisdom that is certain and non-retrogressive, Wherein the teaching of wisdom explains the unalterable causes and temporal characteristics.
You have fully awakened to all gateways of various causes, And you likewise know all gateways of various effects;
To the Tathāgata, the one who has perfectly awakened to all afflictions and their remedies, I prostrate.
With non-dual speech and inexhaustible eloquence, you who skillfully expound the dharma of non-retrogression;
your mind untainted by the eight worldly concerns, I bow my head to you who have reached the shore of merit.
Throughout three asaṃkhyeya kalpas, the Buddha accumulated all practices that are difficult to perform;
moving with a heart of great compassion that universally covers all, he enables both himself and others to cross the stream of afflictions.
Fully understanding the three types of suffering in their utmost subtlety, one gives rise to great compassion out of pity for those who suffer;
within the various natures that are the objects of the three realms, this great compassion extends universally to all places.
Within the Tathāgata’s nature of wisdom there is equality; he regards both enemies and kin with impartiality.
His compassion is vast and immeasurable, universally embracing all classes of sentient beings.
The Buddha preaches a single medicine for all sentient beings, Bringing peace to both physical and mental ailments;
Ultimately, even the most extreme sufferings are dispelled— I prostrate to the one who skillfully expounds this wondrous medicine.
Wholly true and resolute in practice, decisively pure and undefiled Honored One,
you who are certain never again to give rise to defiled dharmas, solely cultivate goodness for the sake of others.
Not seeking one's own benefit from others, having completely renounced all personal pleasure,
through appropriate skillful means and a heart of compassion, they resolutely subdue the diseases of sentient beings.
When sentient beings are ready to be tamed, the Tathāgata knows it perfectly and never misses the moment;
acting as an uninvited friend to all beings, he universally brings them across, giving rise to a heart of compassion.
The Benevolent One skillfully expounds the medicinal Dharma, To treat the root source of the suffering of birth and phenomena.
He illuminates the past and present lives of sentient beings, And fully understands the boundless nature of afflictions;
He eradicates the disease of afflictions in sentient beings, For the Buddha knows the measure of time without any error.
Whatever medicine may suffice to remove a given ailment, the World-Honored One prescribes that medicine accordingly.
All practices undertaken by the Tathāgata are cultivated in accordance with reality until they are perfectly complete;
whether appearing as a single door or as many, he understands their integration with total unimpededness.
The Tathāgata, having fulfilled his merit, has reached the ground of the coolness of all-knowledge;
he is the Honored One who knows the path, recognizes the path, and teaches the path—superior to all paths and toward whom all paths turn.
Rescuing all from the sufferings of saṃsāra, Causing all sentient beings to be free from their bonds,
Universally enabling them to cross the stream of afflictions— To those who are steadfast and fully endowed with shame and remorse.
He is able to firmly plant the holy banner of the Dharma, Manifesting the law that all conditioned phenomena are impermanent;
Revealing the gateway of exhaustion, cessation, and freedom from craving, And displaying the path of tranquility and transcendence.
To him who can skillfully manifest all dharmas, The Honored One who teaches through all dharmas—
To the Great Guide who is able to bring benefit, I bow my head to the one who skillfully bestows joy.
He who constantly speaks words that instruct, benefit, and gladden, Possessing great majesty and great supernormal powers,
The most supreme, pure, and great Brahmā-like Honored One— I bow my head to the Sovereign, the Radiant One.
Having stilled all discourses concerning lineage, And further severed all speech regarding clan,
With even the talk of worldly affairs extinguished, I prostrate to the one who ever speaks the words of the True Dharma.
The Tathāgata’s gait is ever tranquil; He walks with evenness, neither too wide nor too narrow.
Moving in accordance with what is wholesome, those who see him rejoice; This manifests the signs of the Tathāgata’s excellent conduct.
The Tathāgata possesses unshakable right knowledge and vision; he is fully endowed with the nature of his former deeds.
Having accomplished all meritorious works and severed the root of doubt, he enters the village free from the mind of seeking alms.
Upon emerging, he is invariably manifest for all to behold; independent and unswerving, he is the Most Supreme Honored One.
Supremely wondrous and extraordinary, the source of all auspiciousness, Pure and complete in the practice of the Brahma-faring life;
Able to thoroughly understand the phenomena of the five aggregates, And further able to fulfill the seven factors of practice;
Having already been able to destroy the mind of self-conceit, I prostrate to the one who can shatter the net of ignorance.
The Tathāgata has already attained the immovable Dharma, And is further able to fulfill the profound and vast mind;
He is well-able to accomplish the seven noble riches, I bow my head to him who is well-trained in the three trainings.
The Buddha, the Great Being worthy of praise, cannot be terrified by any heterodox or adverse conditions;
having distanced himself from all inauspiciousness, I prostrate to him who has reached the stage of perfect self-mastery.
The holy life is truly well-established; Above, below, and across, all take refuge in it.
Constantly bestowing fearlessness upon sentient beings, I bow my head to the Dharma that is free from grasping.
I take refuge in the Buddha, the Great Arhat, The Honored One whose outflows are all exhausted and untainted;
To him who has accomplished what was to be done and whose virtue is perfectly luminous, To him who has laid down the heavy burden, I prostrate.
Having attained the purpose and benefit of one's own practice, having exhausted all fetters of existence and removed all obscurations,
abiding in right wisdom with a liberated mind— to the one who has emerged and is liberated, I prostrate.
Having realized the principle of wordless liberation, liberated through the exhaustion of craving and grasping,
with a mind free from forgetfulness and perfected in liberation— I bow my head to the one whose mind is free from inversion.

The Buddha’s mind is immeasurable and vast; having well-cultivated his mind through no distinct dharma, he has attained liberation from the bonds of afflictions. I prostrate to him who has destroyed all heterodox classes.
Having exhausted all defiled karma and attained purity, you have realized nirvana without remainder;
O Supreme among Men, Honored One of Liberation, you have conquered the host of Māras in battle.
You are never heedless regarding wholesome dharmas, abiding well in right mindfulness and right wisdom.
You who well open the eye of tranquility to behold all beings, I bow my head to you, the skillful savior from the suffering of birth and death.
You who well awaken beings from the sleep of ignorance, and well shatter the various delusions of sentient beings;
O Buddha, with diligent and courageous resolve, you rouse all those who are indolent.
Among all that is unwholesome, you bestow the wholesome Dharma; among those who have fallen into training, you open the gate of learning;
among those filled with fear, you grant fearlessness; and for those who lack peace, you bring about peace.
Bringing illumination to all that is dark and obscured, Causing the cultivation of goodness within all that is unwholesome,
Giving rise to merit amidst all faults, And eliminating sinful karma within all transgressions;
Causing those who act in opposition to recognize your kindness and virtue, You are able to fulfill whatever the minds of sentient beings desire.
I prostrate to the one who has achieved the reality of mantra-vidyā and practice; I bow my head to the one who can destroy afflictions.
The Buddha has already distanced himself from all deceptions and delusions; His mind is free from agitation and does not become haughty.
The Honored and Victorious One reveals the gate of auspiciousness; I prostrate to the Buddha, the source from which merit arises.
Within a single kṣetra, all practices are born; It is not shared with any other types of supernatural powers.
Ultimately accomplishing the supreme gateway, In all places, it is free from non-sensical expressions.
All doubts and miscellaneous discourses— The definitive, correct speech can utterly destroy them.
Equally cultivating all auspicious practices, you well understand the intentions of all sentient beings.
Having already subdued the speech of others, like a fierce fire consuming dry wood, so too do you burn away all afflictions;
I bow my head to the True Being abiding in the Dharma.
Possessing all auspiciousness and endowed with shame and modesty, The Sovereign of the World, the Supreme Silence,
Śākyamuni, the Great Teacher, Of the Aṅgīrasa Gautama clan,
Who has departed from the darkness of afflictions and delusion, And out of compassion universally gathers all sentient beings.
Constantly engaged in gathering and benefiting others, he is fully endowed with vast and manifold sublime practices.
Regarding all classes of sentient beings and all their superior activities,
the Buddha constantly observes them with great wisdom and universally amasses all that brings benefit to the world.
Possessing the six supernormal powers and the wisdom of subduing, The wisdom of virtue, the wisdom of speech, and the wisdom of timing;
The supreme supernormal powers that counteract all [afflictions], And the wisdom regarding realms, destinies, inclinations, and karmic obstructions.
Possessing the most supreme eloquence and endowed with supernormal powers, you skillfully transform and guide beings through the three modes of discipline;
you are perfectly proficient in understanding all words and meanings—homage to you, whose wisdom of eloquence is inexhaustible.
The Buddha has fully perfected eloquence as described; He has excellently fulfilled all practices and reached the other shore.
With all merits and liberations complete, He manifests a supreme body and pure mind;
Those who hear the Buddha’s voice rejoice in their hearts.
Not falling into any verbal expressions, not grasping at the marks of one's own virtues,
they first realize the primordial path with equanimity.
Capable of bearing the great burden of sentient beings, they attain tranquility amidst all marks.
Having perfected great compassion and other virtues, you have never been apart from the practice of equanimity;
with right wisdom you gather in sentient beings, observing them throughout the long night.
The Tathāgata constantly arouses great valor, Teaching all sentient beings through various virtuous practices;
Furthermore, among all sentient beings, He has already attained a compassionate mind of perfect equanimity.
The Buddha is the one who compassionately pities the world; He has perfectly understood the ultimate truth (*paramārthasatya*).
The Tathāgata’s three eyes are already fully clear and bright, And he is thoroughly endowed with the three kinds of praise.
The Tathāgata has already perfected the three kinds of non-protection, manifesting as the stainless Honored One of the triple world.
Having extensively mastered the practice of the four foundations of mindfulness, he is one who possesses mastery over the bodies of names, phrases, and syllables.
His skillful and inexhaustible eloquence accords with his will, and he has fully penetrated all wisdom for teaching and revealing.
Skilled in understanding the various modes of speech, their eloquence is everywhere unimpeded;
they turn those who are hostile toward them into those who are favorable, and bring purity to those who are full of anger;
they give rise to a heart of reverence amidst all forms of pride, and utterly renounce all matters of profit and gain.
Your conduct is upright and true, most supreme; through your own power, you have realized the state of the Honored One.
You purify all gateways of speech; I bow my head to you who are unattached in language.
Uttering words of welcome that accord with the truth, Fully endowed with all right conduct, The Tathāgata is perfected in all virtues; I prostrate to the one whose dharma is never lost.
Supreme benefactor and sublime tamer, who rejoices in compassion for all sentient beings;
with firm compassion, you desire to benefit others—to you, who ever seek their welfare and happiness, I prostrate.
The Buddha possesses great kindness and virtue toward sentient beings; he is their constant virtuous friend and wise counselor.
Like a father and like a mother, he is able to give birth [to them], desiring that all beings attain wholesome happiness.
The Buddha is the spiritual teacher of all sentient beings; He skillfully expounds the teachings on the ultimate nature of all phenomena.
Proclaiming the supreme meaning according to reality, He causes them to realize the nature of all things.
The Tathāgata always speaks with non-attachment, Skillfully praising what neither increases nor decreases;
His great compassion arises in uninterrupted succession— I prostrate to the one who clearly perceives what is possible and what is impossible.
Praise of the Auspicious Qualities of the Buddha, Middle Volume;
Praise of the Auspicious Qualities of the Buddha, Lower Volume.
Composed by the Venerable Śāntimitra.
I take refuge in the Great Lion’s Roar, who brings forth all gateways of virtuous conduct;
Who knows all natures as they truly are, whose unsurpassed knowledge and vision pervade everywhere;
Who skillfully transforms sentient beings without interruption, proclaiming infinite Dharma gates.
Foremost in breaking the egg of ignorance, He who awakens to all phenomena.
The Great Being who fully realizes sentient beings, The Honored One who awakens to the subtle and wondrous dharmas;
One who has clearly awakened to the principle of non-self, And who has skillfully awakened to the intrinsic nature of all karma.
One who has awakened to the dimensions of all realms, Who thoroughly knows the fundamental nature of arising and ceasing,
Who understands all phenomena of suffering as they truly are, And who has skillfully realized the true self-nature.
Skillfully awakened and free from affliction, you have fully realized the intrinsic nature of the world;
with wisdom opened and clarified, you have shattered all evil views and awakened to the entirety of cause and effect.
Having realized the characteristics of transcendence from the three realms, they further cultivate all the most difficult practices;
their bodies never grow weary, yet they do not cling to signs or artifice.
They feel no revulsion toward even minor teachings, ultimately employing skillful means to gather and benefit others, proclaiming the various Dharma gates of the Middle Way.
Excellent is the Honored Śākyamuni; I prostrate and take refuge in the One Worthy of Offerings.
The supreme speaker, the one who dwells in silence, my greatest and most excellent Master, who skillfully gathers the inclinations of all sentient beings, yet grasps at no phenomena whatsoever.
Fully endowed with the one kind of praise, He is well able to accomplish the four means of integration;
He skillfully proclaims the six dharmas of harmonious respect, And has brought the six constant practices to perfection.
Established in profound right knowledge and vision, Attaining the excellence of all meditative absorptions and tranquility,
Without negligence regarding wholesome dharmas, They have realized the path accomplished by former Buddhas.
To the one who has fully realized the profound right path, Who has opened up the light of profound wisdom,
And who has attained awakening upon that path free from vitarka and vicāra— I prostrate to the Tathāgata, the one who has realized it.
The object of knowledge known by the one who possesses the wisdom of total synthesis—subtle and profoundly deep—is fully awakened to;
he reveals the two kinds of nirvāṇa realms and fully realizes all paths to nirvāṇa.
Sentient beings have long given rise to delusions; the Buddha, through skillful means, teaches the non-delusive Dharma.
Sentient beings are submerged in the mire of birth and death; the Buddha extends his hand to receive and deliver them.
Those sentient beings who fall into the evil realms—the Buddha, by the power of his skillful means, rescues and uproots them.
When sentient beings give rise to fears such as birth and so forth, the Buddha leads them to show the place of fearlessness.
Possessing vast and great sovereign power himself, his body manifests the jewels of all forms and appearances;
within him is stored the wondrous, perfect, and luminous jewel of the mind, as he proclaims the incomparable treasure of the True Dharma.
The Buddha cannot be subdued by others; no one at all can oppose him.
He dwells securely in every gate of joy; all the marks of the Buddha are perfectly complete.
As an unsurpassed śramaṇa of true and correct practice, his wisdom is pure like a blooming lotus.
Universally gathering the holy life (*brahmacarya*) without exception, I bow my head to those who have established themselves in the holy life.
Though they are learned in the worldly Vedas, they do not violate any of the teachings of the Noble Dharma;
having washed away all stains of sin, they have attained the supreme, preeminent state.
He is well-able to accomplish the vidyādhara teachings; he is skilled at leading others to the state of peace.
The Teacher reveals the gateway to sublime bliss and acts as a virtuous guide through the wilderness of saṃsāra.
Always free from all darkness and obscurity, With eyes of joy and serenity ever gazing,
The ultimately unstained and pure Honored One, Whose conduct is unmoved by sin or merit, has attained liberation.
Able to contemplate emptiness within one's own body, with craving and views exhausted and free from defilement,
the mind is detached from the perception of all sensory objects, and free from afflictions and conceptual discrimination.
With a mind abiding in tranquility amidst all activities, you attain liberation within the silent Dharma;
O Great Muni of supreme peace, you are entirely pure and untainted.
The merit of the supramundane is already vast; It skillfully spreads the great illumination throughout the world.
One is able to perceive all the illusory objects of the world, Perfecting the conception of all phenomena as true reality.
The ropes of craving are severed and supernormal powers are perfected;
Wisdom’s great radiance is skillfully brought forth, shattering all hearts of attachment; All mental inclinations are thus rendered utterly tranquil.
The Tathāgata has already abandoned all faults; he is worthy of veneration and offerings.
All unbeneficial and evil dharmas have been eliminated, and he is endowed with every form of benefit.

The Buddha is the virtuous friend of all sentient beings; the foremost among those without feet and those with two feet, he dwells securely within mindfulness, wisdom, and all natures, being perfectly endowed with the quality of non-forgetfulness.
The Buddha, regarding the intrinsic nature of meaning and non-meaning, Abides in their synthesis without attachment;
having eliminated the fear of this shore of birth and death, He is able to realize the bliss of the other shore of nirvana.
The Buddha well abides in and practices the true path; his hearing is unerring and his mind never diminishes.
Among all who are pure, the Buddha is most supreme, his vast physical marks illuminated by the light of wisdom.
Regarding all the flavors of sensual indulgence in the world, the Buddha’s wisdom has long since transcended them;
he praises with wisdom the gateway to Nirvana—homage to the Tathāgata who speaks with certainty.
Untainted view and untainted intention, Untainted speech and untainted action,
Untainted livelihood and untainted diligence, Untainted mindfulness and untainted concentration.
Liberated and undefiled, with wisdom free from defilement, He dwells securely in virtue, concentration, and wisdom;
All fetters and bonds are completely severed, And he has shattered the abodes of afflictions and inversions.
Born from the Brahma-conduct of the Tathāgata, He abides in the supreme stage of cool tranquility;
The Honored One whose every action is serene Is unattached to worldly matters of honor or affection.
Having already been able to sever the fivefold fetters, And further being able to fulfill the sixfold dharmas,
One gives rise to a single mind of impartial protective mindfulness, Accomplishing the four reliances without deficiency.
Pure, singular, and truly without distinction, Equanimously renouncing all that the world cherishes,
With an unerring mind of authentic reflection, One has attained all-pervading pliancy.
With mind well-liberated and liberated through wisdom, Perfectly established in the singular pure conduct—
To the Tathāgata, the supreme and most excellent of beings, I therefore pay homage and offer extensive praise.
I prostrate to the supreme Great Arhat, Who is free from names, free from marks, and free from states;
Who has transcended the gates of names, marks, and states, And for whom names, marks, and states are all utterly tranquil.
He who clearly perceives the mind can extinguish the flames of desire; The stains of craving and attachment toward objects of desire are all removed.
Having abandoned all latent tendencies toward sensual desires, and being free from every fault of desire,
you have skillfully cultivated the sevenfold contemplations and excellently expounded the gates of the factors of enlightenment;
having completely overcome all others, the Buddha is the courageous one who knows no fear.
Free from delusion and having severed defilements, most excellent among the excellent; with the power of precepts prevailing, one is free from fault.
Possessing virtuous wisdom and a subtle mind, one internally gathers various meritorious practices.
Without doubt and free from defilement, always content; having stilled all worldly sources of delusion.
The great task of the Great Śramaṇa has been accomplished; I bow my head to the one who is true and joyful.
The Buddha is the most excellent among the Mānuṣyas; he has thoroughly observed his own body.
Having attained all that is to be attained through the various gates of teaching, I bow my head to the Tathāgata, who is beyond comparison.
With right mindfulness, you perceive all things with supreme insight; unsubdued by others, you are able to subdue them.
Having attained tranquility, you have no further purpose to fulfill; I prostrate to the Bull-King, the Most Exalted One.
Immeasurably profound, abiding in silent stillness, With right wisdom, you always practice the conduct of peace and bliss;
With wondrous deportment in accordance with the Dharma and Vinaya, I bow my head to you whose body is adorned and whose mind is tranquil.

All conditioned phenomena are perfectly complete, and your speech is well-expounded; your body manifests the appearance of the difficult practices of *dhūta*, and your words are free from conceptual proliferation as you abide in the true and real.
I prostrate to the Master of Right Livelihood who is free from craving.
The Tathāgata is most honored, supreme, and sovereign, Just as Śakra is the victor among the gods;
He proceeds with rectitude and observes with skill, His speech is humble, harmonious, and beautiful.
All-pure and utterly purified, Wholly lovely, unattached, and vastly pure;
Filled with the fragrance of matured merit— I prostrate to you who have reached the supreme state.
The Buddha is the supreme King of Great Sages; having extensively accumulated merit, he is full and never-decreasing.
His pure conduct is perfected and his flattery eliminated; I prostrate to the mass of light of right wisdom.
Body and mind are pure and further light and ease; all adversaries have already been stilled.
O Honored One of Tranquil Wisdom, Vast Wisdom, and Great Wisdom, you block the source of anger and are ever joyful.
Among all persons (pudgala), there is none superior to you; you are immeasurable and free from all attachments.
Having attained mastery over the body of phrases, you are free from doubt; I bow my head to the Well-Gone One, the master of skillful understanding.
Supreme among those who teach and subdue, you are the unsurpassed, lovely light-maker.
Free from seeking, pride, and attachment, I bow my head to the pure one who is without deception.
Having already departed from darkness and obscurity, free from all defilement, you are the most supreme among *pudgalas*;
having attained sublime tranquility and great renown, I prostrate to you who are unattached and unbound.
Long since free from delusion and attachment, with the grasping for signs and the view of self eliminated;
you proclaim the Dharma, excellent in the beginning, middle, and end, with its beautiful phrasing and perfect meaning.
Sentient beings dwell in suffering without weariness; through the Buddha’s skillful means, they are brought to rest.
Sentient beings do not turn toward the gate of liberation; through the Buddha’s skillful means, they are led to transcendence.
The Tathāgata does not abide in the dharma of cessation, but constantly practices salvation to gather in the world.
Furthermore, to the vast gateway of the True Dharma, I prostrate to the one of great wisdom who encompasses all.
Having stilled all false and delusive discriminations, you have skillfully departed from all paths of seeking.
You are the supreme person who subdues all unwholesome dharmas; free from the seven kinds of defilement, you have perfected the holy life (*brahmacarya*).
Just as the sky cannot be stained by mud, he remains pure and constantly relies upon the holy life (*brahmacarya*).
Although he has eliminated defiled phenomena and realized the emptiness of their nature, he transcends all speech and his mind is free from attachment.
The Buddha always dwells securely in the nature of mindfulness of the body; the Buddha’s mind has already transcended the two extremes.
To the Honored One of profound wisdom, deep mystery, and heroic power, whose body is perfected within the gateway of auspiciousness;
I prostrate to the one of inconceivable great compassion, who possesses the sovereign power of all actions,
who assists those who are inferior and weak, and who unfailingly accords with the virtuous and beautiful.
The Buddha possesses a vajra-like adamantine body, born from the locus of ultimate reality;
abiding in all gates of correspondence, he has attained the supreme bliss of great nirvāṇa.
The Tathāgata has already attained the supreme benefit; having renounced his own pleasure, he remains unattached.
He leads and shows the world to the place of peace and security, extensively expounding the Right Path for the sake of all sentient beings.
I take refuge in the Great Awakened Honored One, who has realized the path of perfect enlightenment;
for those who have not practiced the holy life, the Buddha has skillfully established [the way].
The Buddha is the knower of the path, the one who recognizes the path and proclaims the path.
The Buddha is the Honored One of the True Path, the one toward whom all paths turn.
The Buddha is born from illumination; he is likewise born of wisdom, born of meaning, and born of the Dharma, skillfully explaining the clear and definitive meaning.
The one who has emerged from all phenomena, the great lion among men,
the great elephant-king among men, the great royal sage among men,
the one of perfect knowledge among men, the venerable one of wisdom and valor among men.
Unrivaled among men, supreme among men, the most excellent of men, a white lotus among men;
without fear or alarm, without timidity and without dread.
The Buddha is one who has transcended fear; he is fearless and free from the clamor of worldly striving.
Having eliminated the perils of dread, he has severed all fears and calamities.
Having himself emerged from the realm of fear, he causes others likewise to emerge.
Having severed my own fear of calamity, I further cause others to sever it as well;
having crossed the ocean of fear and calamity myself, I further cause others to cross it too.
My body hairs bristle with joy, and my body hairs stand on end in awe.
The Buddha is supreme and peerless, and likewise equal to the unequaled.
His merit is beyond all praise, having transcended all measurement;
it cannot be grasped as a form, nor does it possess any distinct divisions.
The supreme person is unique and without a second;
the Buddha possesses self-arisen wisdom, and there is none equal to him.
Having extensively benefited all sentient beings, I prostrate to the Omniscient One.
Among all devas and humans in the world, Within the realms of Brahmā, Māra, and śramaṇas,
The Buddha is the most supreme and honored, And is moreover unsurpassed.
The Jewel of the Buddha is exceedingly rare, And is likewise difficult to encounter.
The appearance of the Buddha-jewel is truly rare and difficult to encounter.
The Buddha is the vast eye, and he is also the great radiance;
he is the great brilliance that shines with great light, the great lamp, and the great torch of illumination.
Free from darkness, with great blazing radiance, he has already attained the supreme Dharma;
his faculties, powers, and the path of awakening are perfected, not shared with the śrāvakas.
If there were no matter of benefit, the Tathāgata would not have been born.
He does not manifest without benefit, nor does he remain hidden without benefit.
For the sake of benefiting all classes of beings, the Buddha has appeared;
out of compassion for the world, he performs deeds that bring about every kind of profit and happiness.
Among all devas and humans, the Buddha is the one of right view;
by means of the Dharma and Vinaya of the true path, he universally instructs and guides all.
Furthermore, among all assemblies, the Buddha is the beloved and honored one.
All shall give rise to a heart of reverence and love, cultivating the visualization of respect;
the Buddha is that which is to be approached, as well as followed and honored.
Prostrating, one beholds Suchness, the most supreme and auspicious jewel.
The Buddha’s eye of wisdom is radiant light, which in turn arises from the eye of wisdom;
it unfolds the brilliance of the flames of wisdom, holding aloft the vast torch of wisdom.
It kindles the lamp of wisdom to shine everywhere, and with great wisdom, it shatters all darkness.
The Tathāgata fully illuminates and understands the intrinsic nature of all phenomena;
the Tathāgata’s faculty of supreme wisdom is subtle, wondrous, and most excellent.
By the power of the Tathāgata’s great wisdom, he cannot be overcome or subdued.
Accumulating the inexhaustible wealth of wisdom, Possessing the priceless jewel of wisdom,
Wielding the keen blade of wisdom, Grasping the superior weaponry of wisdom,
Brandishing the sharp sword of wisdom— Wisdom neither falls nor diminishes.
The Buddha has skillfully opened up right wisdom, awakening to the understanding of all phenomena;
with vast wisdom as his palace, the one of true knowledge dwells therein.
With firm wisdom as his walls, he guards it closely on all sides.
Inconceivable right wisdom serves as the stairway for advancement.
The Victorious One, supreme and unsubdued, dwells with a mind free from distraction;
he is not overcome by others, nor does he subdue anything, for he has nothing to grasp.
Within the three realms, he is one who should be venerated by all.
He observes everything with direct insight and remains entirely unattached.
That which was to be known, he has already known; that which was to be abandoned, he has already abandoned.
That which was to be attained has been attained; the supreme task has been accomplished;
his own business is entirely complete, and he acts as a teacher for the world.
The Buddha is a Great Sage; his diligence is truly unprecedented.
Having established pure, rare, and vast conduct,
you have realized the supreme path; having attained the rare and inconceivable Dharma and secured the highest state, you drink the nectar of nirvāṇa.
Having uprooted the root of the net of craving and severed the source of all faults, his virtuous conduct is without distinction; there is no defiled dharma by which he could be attached.
Born of goodness and possessing a virtuous nature, he has gone forth as a superior and noble renunciant.
I bow my head to the one from whom the roots of goodness originate, the one who has come with excellence.
Unshakable and inconceivable, the wise one is the most honored among the wise;
having removed the stains of deceit and crookedness, he has already crossed the ocean of afflictions.
Through practice in accordance with the Dharma, one is liberated; liberated from all fetters and bonds,
having attained a mind free of grasping, having exhausted all outflows (*āsrava*),
having reached the end of all faults, and having destroyed all poisons.
Having severed all obstacles, he has utterly incinerated the web of all views.
All false and delusive speech, as well as false and delusive sights and sounds,
wrong thoughts, and wrong actions— the Buddha has abandoned them all.
The dharmas of the aggregates, bases, and elements are well-expounded, whether extensively or concisely;
relying on purity and free from bondage, he is supreme among all who rely [on others].
He is a savior for those without a savior, and a refuge for those without a refuge.
For those who have no destination, the Buddha provides a destination.
Having crossed the ocean of birth and death, he enters all realms;
wherever there is a place for manifestation and transformation, he is able to reach them all.
Those who have fallen into the evil realms—the Buddha always knows them and always keeps them in mind;
by means of skillful expedients, he universally delivers and saves them.
Possessing the roots of goodness that are free from greed, free from hatred, and free from delusion, [he acts thus].
The one of great body and eternally abiding body, who brings compassion and benefit;
Clad in the robes of the Śākya clan, he performs vast auspicious deeds;
Possessing rare power of diligence, he is the one of great wisdom and right awareness.
The Dharma of ethical discipline and patience is true; the inner mind is ever-diligent, vast and profoundly deep.
Endowed with all merits, its radiance shines forth greatly; the tamed mind is pure and white.
Like still water, clear and limpid, the seeds of goodness appear in full perfection.
The pure eye of the world is like a blue utpala lotus—
vast and most exquisite— pervading throughout the realms of the ten directions.
The nature of tranquility is moist and supple; The wondrous moon of omniscience, The Buddha’s virtues are vast and boundless; Therefore, I offer this praise.
*Praise of the Auspicious Virtues of the Buddha*, Vol. II.
